facts.text: Belleville earned its name when colonial administrator Sir Francis Gore renamed the settlement in honor of his wife, Lady Annabella Gore, in 1816.
The Ontario Institution for the Education of the Deaf and Dumb, later the Ontario School for the Deaf, began operations in Belleville in the 19th century.
Glanmore National Historic Site, Belleville's community museum, houses restored 1880s rooms and artifacts that chronicle local history.
Belleville gave birth to the Dixie Lee Fried Chicken chain in 1964 and Journey's End Corporation's economy‑limited hotel chain in 1978.
Henry Corby, a 19th‑century merchant, founded Corby Distillery, built a grocery store, and helped fund Belleville's first bridge across the Bay of Quinte.
